Pins, balls and the package

You will learn

How the signals of your design reach the outside world.

A chip sits in a package: on our AX7203 board the XC7A200T is in the 484-ball FBG484. The pin map draws the same die in the 676-ball FGG676 package of the Wukong board. Some balls carry power or configuration and only some are user IO, grouped into banks with their own voltage. A constraints file (XDC) says which ball each signal of your design uses. Put a signal on a ball that is not user IO and the build fails, or worse, the board does not do what you think.

Try it

Search for a ball name like E3, then colour by pin type and find a ball that is not user IO. The spec frame pins a small design to another package, the XC7A100T in CSG324: find the test that puts its clock on ball E3, and the one that counts its pins.
